claim: A counterbalanced two-run full C1-C8 same-host repeat finds that the published hipEngine C5/C6/C8 prefill deficits are stale, not current optimization targets. hipEngine measures 440.200/457.406/473.754 prompt tok/s versus the strongest repeated current/Laurent peer means 316.711/357.259/405.406: +38.99%/+28.03%/+16.86%. The worst hipEngine run still leads the best peer run by +35.83%/+26.73%/+12.14%, and every category plus heldout scope leads at all three widths.

protocol.sampling: greedy; temperature=0, top_k=1, top_p=1, seed=1 for llama.cpp
protocol.timing: per-prompt barrier-to-last-completion complete wall, summed across ten prompts; prompt tokens divided by total wall
protocol.aggregation: arithmetic mean of the two independently aggregated run rates
protocol.hipengine: resident capacity 8, automatic MTP request mode with expected MTP widths none, production profile, max sequence length 1024

target_width_closure.decision: Close the C5/C6/C8 prefill gaps without kernel work. Current hipEngine leads exceed both repeat variance and every category/heldout gate.

void_attempts: A C5/C6-only current-HIP packet used -np 6 because measured width and server capacity were coupled. It is void and deleted; commit 50adc772f adds independent --parallel 8.
Narrow C5/C6/C8 packets omitted the published C1-C4 same-server sequence and are void/deleted. All retained rows come from complete C1-C8 processes.
limitations: Current-HIP C1-C3 and C6 and Laurent C3/C8 show material two-run spread; means and per-run samples are retained rather than selecting the faster run.
The target C5/C6/C8 conclusion is robust to that spread because the worst hipEngine run beats the best peer run at each width.
This is a deployable-configuration comparison: hipEngine production uses BF16 KV and llama.cpp uses F16 KV.
No kernel or runtime change is attributed to this refresh; it measures the accumulated current tree and closes stale scoreboard targets.
